experiment: EXP-A3 — sub-minute freshness-SLA sweep → SLA operating point
verdict: KILL_BRANCH: no adequately-covered sub-minute SLA keeps system_false_allow < 0.01. The only grid points below 0.01 (Δt ≤ 15s) are zero-coverage artifacts (<30 eligible stale serves); wherever caching actually engages (Δt ≥ Nones) system_false_allow ≈ None and ε_emp@p95 already exceeds the declared ε=0.10 (crosses at Δt=30s). ⇒ IEEE-CIS scores must be recomputed in-loop (a cacheable freshness SLA collapses to a few-second re-read window); the certificate stays sound (cert_false_allow=0) throughout.
note: system_false_allow is reported alongside coverage_hit_rate: at sub-minute SLAs only a small fraction of transactions have a same-entity prior read inside the window (few genuine stale serves), so a low system-false-allow reflects both the smaller drift AND the smaller eligible set. The certificate's cert_false_allow stays 0.0 at every Δt (soundness for the declared budget); only the budget-escape term (system_false_allow) moves with the SLA.
